top_categories.workout_context: Road-specific control matters at Tour of the Peak. Practice on mixed terrain: use smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 113 miles.
99ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
At Tour of the Peak, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Tour of the Peak's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before May.
At mile 60 of 113, glycogen is gone. This workout teaches your body to produce watts on fumes.
11,175ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Tour of the Peak. Train it until it feels boring.
11,175ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.
Brief efforts above sustainable power can come from grade changes, positioning, or closing a gap at Tour of the Peak. Train them without letting those efforts derail the longer pacing plan.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 113 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
Low-cadence force work supports 11,175ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.
Steeper ramps, positioning, or pace changes on mixed terrain can demand short hard efforts. Practice them without compromising the sustained work that defines the course.

race_overlay.nutrition: Target 60–80g carbs/hour for Tour of the Peak’s 113 miles. Start fueling within the first 30 minutes — early fueling prevents late-race collapse. Bonking at mile 60 is a nutrition failure, not a fitness failure.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Tour of the Peak. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The technical descents at Tour of the Peak demand practice on similar paved roads. Ride mixed terrain at race-day cadence weekly. Practice braking points, corner entry, line choice, and accelerating smoothly out of turns. Confirm tire pressure and equipment before race week.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Road Specific, TT Threshold, and Over Under to prepare you for 113 miles of mixed terrain in Bakewell, Derbyshire, England.
